title: Xeno-interpretability asks whether models use concepts humans cannot name
friendlyTitle: Researchers ask if AI models use ideas people cannot describe
summary: A new conceptual paper argues that language models may contain stable internal distinctions with no adequate human-language equivalent. It proposes an experimental programme for locating, manipulating and linking these model-native representations to behaviour even when researchers cannot fully describe what they mean.
friendlySummary: The paper suggests that an AI model may organise information in ways that do not match any clear human concept. It proposes experiments to find and test these hidden structures.
whyItMatters: Interpretability work usually searches for familiar human concepts inside a model. If useful internal structures fall outside that vocabulary, safety reviews may need to test causal behaviour and interactions directly rather than relying only on readable labels; for now, this is a research agenda, not evidence that such representations have been found.
friendlyWhyItMatters: People may not be able to explain every important pattern inside an AI model with a simple label. Researchers may need to test what a pattern causes, not only what they think it means.
